title: Projects
text:
Academic and applied work
  Projects with a practical purpose.
  
    Explore all six projects. Swipe or use the arrows.
    1 / 6
  
  
    ←
    
      
        01 / Decision support · 2026
        Strategic Decision Support Project
        
          MET AD 715 — Quantitative & Qualitative Decision Making
        
        
          Prepared a managerial decision report evaluating whether a Boston
          restaurant should invest in a $150,000 turnkey 40-barrel microbrewery
          system with eight tanks, on-premise retail sales, and wholesale
          keg distribution.
        
        
          Examined customer segmentation, competitor positioning, pricing
          strategy, production capacity, operating costs, staffing, and
          financial feasibility.
        
        
          Applied SWOT, PESTEL, Porter’s Five Forces, break-even analysis,
          what-if analysis, sensitivity analysis, KPI review, and financial
          statement interpretation across simulation cycles.
        
        
          The stronger alternative projected approximately $4.58 million in
          three-year revenue and $2.07 million in net income, compared with
          $3.85 million in revenue and $1.55 million in net income for the
          weaker alternative.
        
        
          Results are simulation projections, not actual business earnings.
        
      
      
        02 / Python and SQL · 2026
        Data Analytics and Modeling Projects
        MET AD 599 — Python/SQL Business Analytics
        
          Cleaned, prepared, and validated structured datasets using Python
          and pandas. Work included missing-value handling, target-variable
          mapping, categorical encoding, feature selection, and train/test
          splitting.
        
        
          Built scikit-learn workflows using pipelines, OneHotEncoder,
          StandardScaler, polynomial features, cross-validation, and
          GridSearchCV to compare models and reduce manual processing errors.
        
        
          Tested and documented linear regression, logistic regression,
          Ridge, Lasso, KNN, decision tree, and random forest models.
          Evaluated performance using RMSE, accuracy, and business interpretation.
        
        
          Wrote SQL queries using joins, self-joins, grouping, filtering,
          aggregations, views, and date filters to answer business
          reporting questions.
        
      
      
        03 / Financial analysis · 2025
        Financial Analysis and Business Case Projects
        MET AD 632 — Financial Concepts
        
          Applied financial concepts to evaluate revenue, costs, gross profit,
          operating income, net income, budgets, and profitability trends
          across business-case and simulation-based assignments.
        
        
          Connected financial statement logic to business decisions by
          examining how pricing, cost structure, marketing spend, and
          operational assumptions affect profitability and risk.
        
        
          Translated financial analysis into plain-language recommendations
          for non-technical managers, connecting quantitative results with
          practical business guidance.
        
      
      
        04 / Analytics strategy · 2025
        Analytics Strategy and KPI Projects
        MET AD 571 — Business Analytics Foundations
        
          Developed analytics deliverables that defined business problems,
          identified stakeholders, selected performance metrics, organized
          data requirements, and connected analysis to decision-making goals.
        
        
          Applied business frameworks and reporting logic to evaluate
          opportunities, risks, market conditions, and performance gaps
          across class projects.
        
        
          Created management-ready summaries, charts, and recommendations
          that converted analysis into action steps for non-technical
          decision makers.
        
      
      
        05 / Software evaluation · 2026
        ERP Selection, RFP Scoring, and Vendor Evaluation
        
          Build Fellowship — Public-Sector Finance Simulation
        
        
          Built an RFP-style vendor evaluation model for a city finance
          department, using weighted scoring categories for functional
          requirements, technical integration, implementation services,
          pricing, usability, and vendor experience.
        
        
          Designed finance-focused demo questions and scoring criteria
          covering general ledger, budget controls, AP/AR workflows,
          procurement-to-GL integration, audit trails, role-based security,
          and export functionality.
        
        
          Created process-flow logic for ITB/RFP development, advertising,
          proposal intake, committee scoring, shortlisting, demonstrations,
          negotiations, approvals, and contract execution.
        
        
          Translated qualitative requirements into a structured scorecard
          to compare vendors consistently and support a defensible
          recommendation to stakeholders.
        
        
          Academic simulation of a public-sector procurement process.
        
      
    
  
    06 / Team project · In progress · 2026
  
  Insurance Data Engineer Job Market Analysis
  
    MET AD 688 — Big Data and Cloud Analytics · Boston University
  
  
    This ongoing group project analyzes the job market for
    data engineers in the insurance industry, focusing on
    hiring trends, demand, and required skills. Using job-posting
    data, statistical analysis, and visualizations, our team
    explores the skills employers seek and what those findings
    mean for professionals entering the field. The project is
    part of Boston University’s Big Data and Cloud Analytics course.

title: About Me
text:
My background

  Business-minded. Technology-curious.

  
    Hey, I’m Haben! Originally from Tigray, Ethiopia, I’m now
    based in Boston and pursuing an M.S. in Business Analytics
    at Boston University, with expected graduation in June 2027.
    My path has taken me from studying management at Sheba
    University College to computer science at Bunker Hill
    Community College, and now to exploring how data can guide
    business decisions. I enjoy working through practical
    problems, learning how things work, and turning what I learn
    into something useful. Through academic projects, I’m building
    my skills in Python, SQL, data visualization, and cloud
    technology. My experience in document operations at Ascensus
    and customer service at ABM has taught me to pay attention
    to details and communicate clearly. This portfolio is where
    I share my work, what I’m learning, and my progress toward
    a career in analytics, business intelligence, or data
    engineering.
